subtitle: Wavetable Spectral Filter
tagline: Turns wavetable frames into filter responses: choose from 120 factory tables or draw your own, morph through 256 frames, and set the phase, contour, and motion.

body.lead: TB Filter Table uses wavetables as filters. Each table is a sequence of single-cycle frames on a 256-slot rail, and the current frame is turned into an FIR filter response that shapes your audio. Moving through the frames morphs the filter, from gentle contours to formants, notches, combs, and hard pulse shapes.

body.p: `CUTOFF (H24)` places the frame on the frequency axis, `RESONANCE` sets the contour depth, `FRAME` and the MORPH LFO move through the table, `PHASE` sets the phase response, and `MIX` blends with the latency-compensated dry signal. The EDIT view adds `DRIVE`, the plugin presets, and tools for drawing and capturing your own custom table.

ul: 120 factory tables in 10 families, plus an editable CUSTOM table
256-slot frame rail; tables morph smoothly or in steps between 2 to 256 keyframes
CUTOFF (H24) from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, with an effective floor of 200 Hz
RESONANCE contour depth from flat (−100%) to squared (+100%)
Four phase modes: MINIMUM, LINEAR, ORIGINAL, and RAW
MORPH LFO with six shapes, ±100% range, and a 0.01 to 10 Hz rate
Custom table drawing, frame capture, and .tbft table files
20 factory presets, user presets, undo, and redo

steps: Frame from TABLE, FRAME, and MORPH LFO

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Filter Table 1.1.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build (AU and VST3) is version 1.0.1 and may differ.

ol: Insert TB Filter Table on a synth, pad, drum, vocal, or bus track. The Init preset uses the Moving Formant table, `FRAME` 129, `CUTOFF` 4 kHz, `RESONANCE` +15%, and `MIX` 75%.
Choose a table with the table selector {{4}}, or step through all tables with its arrows.
Sweep `FRAME` {{6}} to morph through the table, and move `CUTOFF` {{7}} to place the response.
Set the depth with `RESONANCE` {{8}} and the balance with `MIX` {{9}}.
For movement, choose a `TYPE` in the MORPH LFO row {{10}}, then set `RANGE` and `RATE`.

body.p: The main view holds the everyday controls. `EDIT` {{5}} opens the secondary tools, and `DONE` {{13}} returns to the main view.

rows: CUSTOM or 120 factory tables · Moving Formant
Chooses the set of frames the filter morphs through. A new table changes both the tone and the meaning of every frame position.
Base position on the table's 256-slot rail; the filter morphs continuously as it moves. Positive RANGE moves upward from here; negative RANGE moves downward to here.
The frequency assigned to harmonic 24 of the frame. At 4 kHz the frame spans 20 Hz to 20.48 kHz across ten octaves. The effective cutoff does not go below 200 Hz; lower settings act as 200 Hz.
Contour depth: −100% is flat, 0% follows the table, and +100% squares it. In RAW mode it sets how far the kernel departs from a neutral one. High values create strong peaks and ringing.
The phase response of the filter. ORIGINAL keeps the phase of the source frame; RAW uses the frame waveform itself as the filter kernel.
Post-filter nonlinear color. At 0 dB it is bypassed exactly, without adding a static cut. Drive can raise the level.
Blends the filtered signal with the latency-compensated dry signal.
OFF, SINE, TRI, SAW, SQR, RND · OFF
The frame LFO shape. RND is a random sample-and-hold.
Directional morph span: +100% moves up to 256 slots above FRAME, −100% moves up to 256 slots below it, and 0% stops frame movement.
Free-running LFO rate. It does not follow the host tempo.

body.p: In the EDIT view, the FRAME LFO tab shows the same TYPE, RANGE, and RATE controls. TB Filter Table also has a host Bypass parameter, and it reports a fixed latency of 128 samples (about 2.7 ms at 48 kHz) in every phase mode.

tip.text: The phase modes change how transients and stereo content behave. Compare them on drums, and check the result in mono.

body.p: The CUSTOM entry at the start of the table list is your own editable table. Build it in the EDIT view with the TABLE TOOLS tab.

rows: Resets the custom table to a new two-keyframe starting table.
Copies the currently rendered frame into the same slot of the custom table.
Removes the selected authored keyframe from the custom table.
Drag inside the current waveform panel, then release to commit the drawn frame.
IMPORT TABLE FILE... and EXPORT CUSTOM TABLE... read and write .tbft table files. Table files are separate from plugin presets.
SMOOTH interpolates continuously between adjacent keyframes; STEPPED switches between them without interpolation. The keyframe status shows which applies.

body.p: Plugin presets store all settings. Choose them in the PRESET / HISTORY row of the EDIT view, or step with its arrows. Save asks for a name and stores a user preset in Documents/TB Filter Table/Presets/User. UNDO and REDO step through editable actions.

body.p: Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Vowel pad
recipes.use: Slow, talking motion on pads and drones.
steps: Lower MIX if the vowel motion is too strong.

recipes.title: Drum contour
recipes.use: A moving notch that keeps drum attacks clear.
steps: Compare the PHASE modes and keep the one with the cleanest attack.

recipes.title: Bus color
recipes.use: A gentle spectral shape on a group or mix bus.
steps: Sweep FRAME slowly to find the most flattering contour.

recipes.title: Deliberate damage
steps: Watch the output level; DRIVE adds level.

rows: CUTOFF has no effect below 200 Hz.
The effective cutoff stops at 200 Hz; settings from 20 to 200 Hz act as 200 Hz.
Lower RESONANCE, or choose a smoother table or frame.
Lower RATE or RANGE. Fast frame movement can create modulation artifacts.
Compare the PHASE modes and keep the one with the cleanest attack.
Lower DRIVE or MIX, and match levels before comparing.
The LFO does not follow the tempo.
RATE is free-running. Set it by ear.

Restored the published 20 Hz to 20 kHz Cutoff automation mapping while keeping the 200 Hz effective floor; every public parameter ID and the state schema are unchanged.
First release: 120 factory tables with 2 to 256 keyframes for morphable spectral filtering; four phase modes, bounded spectral contours, nonlinear drive, and a Frame LFO.
